lines.text: Ina kwana? [Good morning?] You greet well. Good child.
Ẹ káàárọ̀! [Good morning!] How's school?
Sannu da aiki! [Well done with your work!]
Nnọọ! [Welcome!] Come and sit small.
Light don go again! Bring the lantern, the real one!
No light, no fan, no TV. Then let's tell stories.
Rain! The clothes! Children, the clothes!
This heat. Even the goats are queueing for shade.
The tailor said Thursday. Which Thursday? He's a philosopher.
Bread went up again. Even the bread is surprised.
In my time, that clock worked. In my time, many things worked.
My son, come and help me carry this. Your back is young.
Generator noise everywhere! Who can hear the radio?
Welder! Welder! He's not here. He is 'coming'.
I took my shoe to the cobbler. Now he's renting it back to me.
That pothole has been there since my wedding. It's family now.
Children! Out of the road! Okada is not a toy!
These students, always running. Where is everybody going?
Grinding machine! Pepper, tomatoes! Bring your bowl!
Lock your doors. Not for thieves. For mosquitoes.
The old man in the university garden? He greets well. That's all I know.
Every evening NEPA takes light. We've stopped being angry. Mostly.
The new mall: big glass, big lights. Our street is still dark.
Somebody is tapping wires at night. My meter is crying.
The students who stayed for the strike help everybody. Good children.
My tailor has no customers. He's sewing his own trousers.
Everybody's pointing a phone at everybody. Then who is living?
Election posters on my wall. I didn't agree. My wall did.
These students came small. Now look. Gowns. Ahh, time.
The town feels brighter. More lamps on the road. Somebody did something.
Freshers in town! Hold your bags well. The market is a teacher.
Exam season. Students buying Brain Booster Tea like medicine.
My neighbour's son passed! He's dancing in the road. Let him.
Allowance day. The market will be loud tonight. Good for business.
Thursday! I've been awake since four, ready to bargain.
Strike again? In my day— well, also strike. Same.
The whole town is shouting for the university. Who else?
Candidates. Promise everything, deliver pamphlets.
Convocation. Tailors haven't slept. Everything is 'Thursday'.
Iftar at my house today. Come, there's enough.
Merry Christmas! Come and eat rice. Don't say no.
In my time, Valentine was called 'go and greet her father'.
Harmattan. Wear a sweater. Yes, you. I can see you shivering.
